seo.title: Ari Cummings — software developer

lines: Operating systems from the kernel up.
hero.intro: I design and build secure communication, systems software, and the infrastructure underneath it — mostly in Rust, C# and TypeScript.

paras: I'm Ari Cummings. I write software across the whole stack: an encrypted messenger designed to survive targeted surveillance, a Rust operating system with its own network stack and text browser, a multithreaded Minecraft server, and the Linux infrastructure that runs all of it.

I'm from McMinnville, Oregon, studied at The Delphian School, and I'm studying computer science in college. Client work keeps me honest: production booking and membership platforms for real businesses, from database to deployment.
Everything source-available on this site is AGPL or GPL. Fork it.

page:home.clientIntro: Alongside my own projects I build and maintain production platforms for small businesses — a 24/7 trailer-rental booking system and a riding-methodology membership site.

work:enclave.title: Enclave
work:enclave.summary: An open-source messenger with the features people expect from Signal — chats, groups, voice and video calls, photos, voice notes, reactions, disappearing messages — and a much stronger design against surveillance.

sections.heading: Post-quantum from the first message
sections.html: Every session combines three independent key-exchange families — X448, ML-KEM-1024 and Classic McEliece-8192128 — and every ratchet turn takes a full post-quantum step.

sections.heading: Metadata hidden, not just content
sections.html: Traffic goes through Tor to each server's onion service (the Nym mixnet is optional), every message is the same size, and constant-rate cover traffic hides when you are talking. Servers never learn who writes to whom.

sections.heading: No phone number, no email
sections.html: Your account is a key. Usernames are optional and checked by public key-transparency logs with independent witnesses.

sections.heading: No trusted server
sections.html: Anyone can run one; none of them can read messages, see your contacts or change your keys without being caught. It's Rust everywhere possible, including the UI.

sections.heading: Where it stands
sections.html: The protocol, the servers, the network layer, the desktop app and the release pipeline are built and tested in CI; Android and iOS are being built. Enclave has not been audited yet: don't rely on it to protect anyone until it has.

work:rustos.title: RustOS
work:rustos.summary: An x86-64 operating system written in Rust: a preemptive SMP kernel with ring-3 processes, a Linux-compatible system-call ABI, NVMe/AHCI/USB storage, FAT and ext2/3/4 filesystems, a full USB stack, an in-tree TCP/IP stack with wired, USB and Intel Wi-Fi 6E drivers, HTTPS, a POSIX-like shell and a small userland — all booted by UEFI.

sections.heading: The kernel
sections.html: Per-process address spaces with demand paging, copy-on-write fork, clone threads with futexes, a per-CPU scheduler with affinity, execve of static, PIE and dynamically linked ELF programs, POSIX signals and job control, and around 180 Linux system calls — across all cores, with IPI TLB shootdown.

sections.heading: Storage and USB
sections.html: NVMe, AHCI, virtio-blk and USB mass storage; GPT/MBR; FAT12/16/32 read/write and ext2/ext3/ext4 read/write with jbd2 journal replay, extents and metadata checksums. The USB stack is interrupt-driven xHCI with hot-plug, hubs, bulk streams, HID report parsing and USB Attached SCSI.

sections.heading: Networking
sections.html: An in-tree TCP/IP stack with DHCP, DNS, BSD sockets and drivers for Intel and Realtek NICs plus Intel AX210 Wi-Fi with WPA2-PSK and WPA3-SAE, over IPv4 and IPv6. wget speaks TLS 1.2/1.3, and browse is a lynx-like text browser with CSS layout, JavaScript (QuickJS-ng), forms, cookies, HTTPS and a graphical mode.

sections.heading: Userland
sections.html: init, a POSIX-like shell, rbox (about 90 coreutils), four virtual consoles and pseudo-terminals. Upstream musl builds into a sysroot, so BusyBox, curl and the QuickJS engine compile and run unchanged.

sections.heading: Where it began
sections.html: Built on the foundation of Philipp Oppermann's Writing an OS in Rust and grown well beyond it.

work:multiforge.title: MultiForge
work:multiforge.summary: A free-software, Folia-style regionized multithreaded drop-in replacement for the NeoForge dedicated Minecraft server. Swap your neoforge server jar for MultiForge's; your existing world, mods, configs and launch command keep working, and the world ticks in parallel across ownership regions.

sections.heading: How it parallelizes
sections.html: Loaded chunks group into regions; each tick, every region runs its random ticks, scheduled ticks, block events, entities and block entities on a worker, in parallel, while the server thread keeps running Vanilla's loop and waits at a barrier. A mod call that reaches into another region is rerouted to the owner, and mods classified legacy run one at a time — so no mod needs to opt in.

sections.heading: Verified, not promised
sections.html: Every NeoForge GameTest plus MultiForge's own region-tick tests pass; a vanilla-parity gate ticks one fixed-seed world on stock NeoForge and on MultiForge (1 and 4 workers) and expects identical output, chunk for chunk; live scenarios cover cross-region teleports, a raid, the dragon fight and fixture mods that write across regions; a strict-mode swarm of real protocol clients runs with zero ownership violations.

sections.heading: Status
sections.html: Pre-release, based on NeoForge 21.1.251 (Minecraft 1.21.1). Install needs JDK 21; in-game commands resize the worker pool and report MSPT live. All under GPL-3 — no token, no activation, no phone-home.

work:edex.title: eDEX
work:edex.summary: A sci-fi desktop shell for Hyprland written in Rust and drawn with wgpu, and the privacy-focused Linux distribution whose desktop it is: eDEX-DE and eDEX-OS.

sections.heading: The shell — eDEX-DE
sections.html: Hyprland tiles your applications; eDEX-DE draws everything around them: a multi-tab terminal on alacritty_terminal, a file browser, a system dashboard with privacy indicators for Tor, Tailscale, VPN, microphone and camera, an on-screen keyboard, a launcher, 14 settings categories wired to real backends, notifications, a power menu and a greetd login screen. Thirteen themes ship built in, the config live-reloads, and an IPC drives the shell from key bindings.

sections.heading: The distribution — eDEX-OS
sections.html: A privacy-focused, performance-tuned Linux distribution based on CachyOS (Arch) whose desktop is eDEX-DE. Tor transparent mode redirects all TCP and DNS through Tor with a fail-closed nftables policy that rolls back if Tor cannot bootstrap; Tailscale, WireGuard and OpenVPN are built in; dnscrypt-proxy resolves with DNSSEC and no logging; MAC randomisation and kernel hardening are on by default; the Calamares installer does btrfs subvolumes and LUKS.
